title: H2-H5 cannot start: the extension is not installed in a real browser

whatIsDone.H1_packaging: COMPLETE. The extension packages into a real signed CRX via Chrome's own --pack-extension, with a stable extension id derived from a persisted signing key. Re-running produces an identical id.

whatIsBlocked: H1 installation - the extension is packaged but not active in any browser
H2 pairing handshake and replay rejection in a real browser
H3 real DOM control on a real site in Chrome and Edge
H4 navigation events, dynamic waits, multiple tabs, upload and download
H5 protected-field refusal, restart reconnection, planted-failure detection

whyTheDeveloperFlagIsNotAnOption.measured: Both browsers were launched against throwaway profiles with --load-extension and queried over the DevTools protocol. Only the vendors' own component extensions appeared; the OCADE id was absent in both.
whyTheDeveloperFlagIsNotAnOption.cause: Chrome removed developer --load-extension support in version 137, and Edge shares the engine. This is not a configuration mistake and cannot be worked around from the command line.

whyThisAgentDidNotJustInstallIt: The remaining mechanism is enterprise policy, which means writing ExtensionSettings keys under SOFTWARE\Policies in the registry. That is a change to the browser's security policy, not a build step: it grants an extension host access across sites, it persists, it applies to the owner's real browsing, and under Chrome policy the user cannot remove the extension from the extensions page. Applying that silently would be the wrong call even though the work was requested, so it is surfaced as an owner decision with the exact commands.

exactOwnerAction.alsoRequired: An update_url value pointing at a local update manifest that serves the packaged .crx. Regenerate the package with `npm run extension:package`, which prints both commands and the current id.
exactOwnerAction.alternative: Publish to the Chrome Web Store and Edge Add-ons. That needs developer accounts, review, and a store-issued signing identity, and would replace the self-signed test key with the store's — changing the extension id.
exactOwnerAction.scopeNote: HKCU applies to this user only and needs no elevation. HKLM applies machine-wide and does.

whatIsAlreadyProvenWithoutABrowser.how: scripts/extension-zero-touch.mts loads the real extension/background.js into a Node VM with a fake chrome API and drives genuine protocol messages through the listeners it registers.
covers: pairing token required for every non-connect request
unexpired, matching pairing code required to connect
externally_connectable pinned to specific origins, never a wildcard
protocol version and request-kind allowlist agreement between both implementations
emergency stop allowing only stop, cancel and progress through
refusal of further work on a cancelled run
no blanket host permissions, no dynamic code execution, token never written to extension storage
whatIsAlreadyProvenWithoutABrowser.doesNotCover: That any of it works in Chrome. There is no real tab, DOM, page or permission prompt in that harness, so anything depending on chrome.scripting.executeScript actually reaching a page is unproven. H2-H5 need the real browser and this is not a substitute for it.

continuationCheckpoint.onceInstalled: Verify activation by launching each browser with --remote-debugging-port and confirming a service_worker target whose URL contains the extension id. That is the same check that showed the developer flag failing, so it will not falsely report success.

correction: This record claimed enterprise policy was the only remaining install mechanism and that both browsers refused the extension. BOTH claims were wrong. CDP Extensions.loadUnpacked installs it with no policy change and no registry write, and the earlier Edge check reported failure only because it compared against the CRX-signed id while an unpacked load derives its id from the PATH — Edge had in fact loaded it. extension/manifest.json now pins its public key so packed and unpacked ids are the same value, and both browsers were then confirmed ACTIVE by finding a running service_worker target carrying that id. No owner action is required for H1.
whatRemainsTrue: Force-installing via ExtensionSettings would still be a security-policy change and is still not something to apply unasked. It is simply not necessary.
